quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Rain reduces your ability to see. Slow down and turn on your headlights. If rain is very heavy, pull onto the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid out of control, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes gently.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until the car is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will be very slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means more impairment.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous when driving in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely.
Not watching for workers and moving equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and do not follow vehicles too closely. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop (school buses, trucks with hazardous materials, etc.).
Watch for trains coming from either direction.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings, use extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no trains are coming from either direction. Be aware that school buses and hazardous materials trucks must stop at all crossings.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: In bad weather or darkness, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to hazards.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.
Be ready for anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable and may suddenly change direction. Bicycles and children are small and hard to see, so always be alert.

questions.question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a U-turn (where allowed).

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when it is needed to avoid a crash. Do not use it just because a driver or bicyclist is moving slowly or is in your way.

questions.question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross dashed lines to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Why is it helpful to look far ahead when driving on the highway?

options.text: It helps you keep up with traffic.
It reduces sudden braking or turning.
It helps you spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking ahead helps you avoid sudden stops or quick turns. When you watch the road ahead and stay ready to stop or change lanes, you can drive more safely, use less fuel, and help traffic flow smoothly.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way you would on dry roads.
Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your distance from the car ahead. Your vehicle takes longer to stop than it does on dry roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a school zone is coming. You should slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing the turn.
It lets other drivers know what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before finishing the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, riders, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: What should a worried, nervous, angry, or crying driver do?

options.text: They will drive the same as always.
They can drive faster because they are more alert.
They should calm down and focus before starting the car.
They should call a friend while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should calm down and focus before starting the car.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions make it hard to drive well. When you are worried, upset, angry, or crying, your mind is not on driving. Calm down and get focused before you start driving.

questions.question: Should drivers avoid driving next to large vehicles for long periods of time?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have big blind spots on both sides. Do not drive next to a large vehicle for a long time. It is safer to drop back or move ahead.

questions.question: What happens when a driver is distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
The driver reacts more slowly to dangers.
The driver usually drives faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver reacts more slowly to dangers.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers react slower to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: What should drivers do at a flashing yellow arrow?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
Turn left because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must let them and pedestrians pass first.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they see an animal on the road?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk the horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not startle or scare it.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many types of drugs can make it harder to drive. This includes illegal drugs, prescription medicines, and over-the-counter medicines. It is a crime to drive while impaired by any drug.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at the same speed.
When one lane of traffic moves faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions are more likely when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles on the road. Driving faster than traffic increases your risk of a collision. Driving slower than traffic is also dangerous because it can cause rear-end collisions or make other drivers swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: The intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, but your light is green. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait until the intersection clears before entering.
Follow other vehicles into the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the intersection clears before entering.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if other vehicles are blocking your way, even if your light is green. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light turns red, you will block cross traffic. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space before moving back into the driving lane. Make sure there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the right lane.
